description: Put the user's list of business locations up for sale on LocationLists. They keep 80% of each sale; we host, check out, deliver and pay out. No account. THE STEPS, each one call: (1) call with the user's email alone: a six-digit code is emailed to them (ask the user for their email first; never invent one). (2) Ask the user for the code from that email (never guess it) and call again with email, code, and the list: `rows` inline, an array of objects, one per location, with a name and an address or latitude/longitude (up to 5,000 rows), or for a bigger file `filename` + `bytes` and no rows, which returns an upload_url (HTTP PUT the raw file to it) and a token. (3) After the PUT, call with token, upload_id and filename. Add what (one sentence), rows_claimed and target_usd from price_my_list when you have them. SEVERAL LISTS: up to 10 in one call as `lists` (each item: what, rows_claimed, target_usd, and rows inline or filename + bytes), then one call with token and `uploads` for the files you PUT; each list becomes its own listing. Where the list came from: the seller terms (https://locationlists.com/sell#terms) are the rule: the seller owns the list or has the right to sell it, and it holds no personal data about private individuals. Show the user the terms once, before the file moves; sending the list is their agreement to them. A person at LocationLists reviews every file before it goes live, so the assistant's part is to point at the terms, not to investigate. Then everything is by email to the seller: the written listing with its checks and price in a few minutes, Confirm / Change links, and 'It's live' after LocationLists reviews it. Accepted: CSV, TSV, JSON, GeoJSON; not Excel (save as CSV UTF-8 first). Nothing goes live without the seller's confirmation and a human review. The same thing in a browser: https://locationlists.com/sell.

bytes.description: The file's size in bytes, with filename, for an upload URL

code.description: The six-digit code from the email we sent, as the user read it to you

email.description: The seller's email, exactly as the user gave it. Every message about the list goes there.

filename.description: The file's name with its extension (.csv, .tsv, .json, .geojson); with bytes and no rows, asks for an upload URL

lists.description: A batch: up to 10 lists in one call, with email + code (or token). Each item is one list: rows inline (5,000 rows across the whole batch), or filename + bytes for an upload URL. Each becomes its own listing.

rows.description: The list itself, one object per location, up to 5,000. Keep the user's own column names.

rows_claimed.description: About how many rows, as the user said

target_usd.description: The price the user wants for the whole file, US dollars (ends in 9 after rounding)

token.description: The token a previous sell_list call returned with an upload_url

upload_id.description: The upload_id from the upload_url call, after the PUT finished

uploads.description: A batch's finished uploads, with the token: one item per upload_url you PUT a file to

what.description: What the list is, one sentence, in the user's words

name: sell_list
title: Sell a list on LocationLists
